headline: Good morning, Frankie. The one thing to know before your coffee: the watchdog is still asleep. It sent its last email at 12:36 PM PT yesterday and has not fired once in the ~18 hours since — straight through the PT evening and the entire overnight into this morning. That is the only hourly eye on the only live campaign, and it slept through the window where a kill gate would actually matter. So the honest status of the $300 Plan right now is: unknown. Last confirmed reading is still $205.24 of $300 (68%), 21 leads, $9.77 CPL — the same numbers as the AM brief, because no new data has arrived. We do not know today’s spend, we do not know if a lead came in overnight, and we do not know if a gate should have tripped. Everything else is exactly where the morning left it, which is its own kind of signal after a full day: compliance is 0/7 on day seven of live dialing; the six CA/TX phone numbers from Wednesday are still sitting unpapered; cost per booked call has still never been measured with ~$95 and the $240 notify line ~a day and a half out; and there is still no written word from you anywhere in the mailbox — ten days now. One genuinely good thing: this PM edition reached the disk, the first PM brief to publish in three days (Sep 2 and Sep 3 PM both fired and wrote nothing). So the brief lane is now two-of-four and steadying. Two moves, one each, and they are the same two as this morning because nothing moved them. Frankie: the b3/b7 numbers or the one-line state rule — today was a quiet lead day, which makes it the cheapest possible day to place them. Chitraksh: wake the watchdog and get one clean run out, because a campaign spending unobserved overnight with $95 left and a double-or-kill call coming is the exact situation the watchdog exists to prevent.

There is no fresh data at all: today’s spend, any overnight lead, and whether a gate should have tripped are simply unknown. The last confirmed reading is still $205.24 / 68% / 21 leads.
